source_text: Quae ergo tot blasphemiarum necessitas fuit, si nec ista, quam amplexabaris, fuit? Quae quidem nihil habens momenti, tamen velut quaedam tabula videbatur, quam in tanto naufragio contineres, quam victis remisisti, sero licet, lacertis. Ut enim res repetitione clarescat: ideo Manichaeus credebaris ab ineptis quibusque tolerandus, ne gratiae Christi non in omnibus una efficientia videretur, ad hoc tu nunc sine adactu nostro expositionis tuae processibus intulisti dicens Apostoli sententiam, quae ait: Gratia autem ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n170] , in hominibus quidem maioris aetatis posse, in parvulis vero non posse compleri, sed esse in parvulis aliud brevius exilius egentius, quod licet tu excogites, tamen nequaquam dixisse Apostolum confiteris.
pass_a_gloss: What necessity therefore of so many blasphemies was there, if not even that which you were embracing was? Which indeed, having nothing of moment, nevertheless seemed as a certain plank which you would hold in so great a shipwreck, which, oars having been conquered, you have sent away, though late, from your arms. For that the matter may become clear by repetition: for this reason a Manichaean was believed by any inepts to be tolerable, lest the grace of Christ seem not of one efficiency in all; to this you have now without our driving brought in by the progresses of your exposition, saying that the Apostle's sentence, which says: But grace from many offenses into justification, can indeed be completed in human beings of greater age, but cannot in little children, but that there is in little children another shorter, poorer, more needy thing, which although you think it out, you nevertheless confess the Apostle in no way said.

pass_b_english: What necessity, then, was there for so many blasphemies, if even the necessity you embraced did not exist? Although it had no real weight, it at least seemed like a plank you were holding amid so great a shipwreck. Now, though late, your defeated arms have let it go. To make the matter clear by repetition: all sorts of fools thought you should be tolerated as a Manichaean lest Christ’s grace seem not to have one effect in everyone. Yet without any compulsion from us, the progress of your own explanation has now led you to this: you say that the apostle’s statement, ‘But grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16), can be fulfilled in older people but cannot be fulfilled in infants. In infants there is something else, smaller, thinner, poorer—something which, although you invent it, you confess the apostle never said.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
